What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend exploring the different neighborhoods of Milan, taking day trips to Lake Como or Bergamo, and making the most of Italy’s train network to visit cities like Florence, Venice, and Rome—there’s so much to see just a few hours away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found challenging was the more relaxed attitude toward time and planning—things often started late or were organized last-minute, which required some adjustment coming from a more structured Danish context.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the strong sense of community, the daily social rituals like aperitivo, and the Italian passion for food, art, and conversation—it made everyday life feel vibrant and connected.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be flexible and patient – Things may be less structured than at UCPH, so adaptability is key.

Take initiative – You’ll need to be proactive with course registration, communication, and finding information.

Enjoy the culture – Embrace the Italian lifestyle, try the local food, travel around, and make time for social life—it’s a big part of the experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was stepping out of my comfort zone—meeting new people, adapting to a different academic system, and getting to live and travel in such a culturally rich country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge was adapting to the less structured teaching style and navigating administrative processes. 

Also a lot of italian people do not speak english.
